items.readable_text:
Content:
To construct the standard matrix of a linear transformation [MATH: T] in [MATH: \mathbb{R}^2,] we find the images of the vectors in the standard basis [MATH: \{ \mathbf{i}, \mathbf{j} \}] of [MATH: \mathbb{R}^2] under [MATH: T,] and then use those images as columns in the standard matrix.

Content:
To demonstrate, let's consider the following linear transformation:

Content:
[MATH: [x; y]]

Content:
Computing [MATH: \mathbf T(\mathbf i),] we get

Content:
[MATH: T(i)|= T[1; 0]; = [2 ⋅ 1 − 1 ⋅ 0; 1 + 3 ⋅ 0]; = [2; 1].]

Content:
Computing [MATH: \mathbf T(\mathbf j),] we get

Content:
[MATH: T(j)|= T[0; 1]; = [2 ⋅ 0 − 1 ⋅ 1; 0 + 3 ⋅ 1]; = [− 1; 3].]

Content:
Therefore, the standard matrix for this linear transformation is [MATH: [2|− 1; 1|3]]

Content:
In the diagram below, we see the vectors in the standard basis [MATH: \{ \mathbf{i}, \mathbf{j} \}] of [MATH: \mathbb{R}^2] and their images [MATH: \{ \mathbf{i'}, \mathbf{j'} \}] under the transformation.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/5e11750ccefd14ec2fd05288606f01da]

Content:
In general, a linear transformation in [MATH: \mathbb R^n] has a standard matrix of dimensions [MATH: n \times n,] whose columns are the images of the basis vectors under the action of the linear transformation.

EXPLANATION

Explanation:
Method 1

The images of the vectors in the standard basis [MATH: \{ \mathbf{i}, \mathbf{j} \}] are the first and second columns of [MATH: T,] respectively.

Therefore, we have the following:

[MATH: T(i)|= T[1; 0] = [− 1; 8]; T(j)|= T[0; 1] = [5; 3]]

Method 2

We can find the images of the vectors in the standard basis [MATH: \{ \mathbf{i}, \mathbf{j} \}] by computing the matrix products [MATH: T\cdot\mathbf{i}] and [MATH: T\cdot\mathbf{j}] as follows:
[MATH: T(i)|= T ⋅ i = [− 1|5; 8|3][1; 0] = [− 1; 8]; T(j)|= T ⋅ j = [− 1|5; 8|3][0; 1] = [5; 3]]
